changes: p2 name normalized from 'Surahi' to 'Sura': '-hi' is the vernacular (Apabhraṃśa/Old Hindi) instrumental/agentive ending governing 'likhāpitam'. This agrees with the catalogue's 'Sura Rāuta'. Confidence lowered to medium.
Added a servant_of relation from p2 to p1. 'tacchāsanika' (written tatchāsanika) means 'his officer, one under his command', and 'tat' refers back to Jayacandradeva.
Title 'tacchāsanika' is kept as written. Notes now explain it and record that the scribe is not named.

persons.name: Sura
persons.evidence: tatchāsanikarāutaśrīsurahi ātmārthe idaṃ pustikā 〇 likhāpitam

notes: The colophon names Jayaccandradeva (Jayacandra, the Gāhaḍavāla king) as the reigning king in Vārāṇasī. The era is not named, but VS fits his reign (c. 1170–1194 CE), so VS 1239 ≈ 1182 CE. 'tatchāsanika' = tacchāsanika, 'his (the king's) officer/appointee'. 'rāuta' is a rank title (from rājaputra). 'surahi' is read as Sura plus the vernacular instrumental ending -hi, the agent of 'likhāpitam'; the name Surahi is less likely. The catalogue's 'Scribe: Sura Rāuta' is wrong: Sura had the copy made for himself (commissioner/owner). The actual scribe is not named; 'lekhaka' appears only in the closing benediction. The weekday has not been checked against an ephemeris.
